description:
Outgoing citation edges of one decision: the statute provisions it cites (with how often it cites each — that is the Normenkette, weighted) and the decisions it relies on.

`treatment` is null on every edge and stays null. Classifying an edge as gefolgt / abgegrenzt / aufgegeben is unbuilt work, and a wrong 'aufgegeben' in a brief is worse than no label at all. Read the citing passage yourself with `listCasePassages`.

A decision we can prove exists but do not hold answers `known_missing`, with the decisions that attest it — not a 404.

LANGUAGES (EU decisions). For a decision of the Court of Justice, the General Court or the Civil Service Tribunal we may hold more than one language version: German where the Court has published one, and the English version as the Court published it (never a machine translation). `lang` ('de' or 'en') asks for one; the default is German when it exists, else English. The answer says which language the passages are in (`language`) and which are held (`available_languages`); a language that is not held returns the default with a `language_note`. A decision whose only stored text is the EUR-Lex error page has no text here.

case.description: A juris doknr, an ECLI, or this site's decision URL as `search` returns it.

lang.description: Language of the decision text: 'de' or 'en'. Default: German when it exists, else English.
